_comment: Operator-facing match labels, shared by BOTH language implementations:
OperatorMatchLabel in internal/engine/match_label.go (Go) and the
combination of poolLabel/leagueAwareLabel (viewer_utils.jsx),
poolMatchNumberOf (pool_ids.jsx) and matchLabel (write_result.jsx) that
scoreRowMatchLabel (admin_schedule_score_editor.jsx) already composes for
the score-editor header (JS). TestOperatorMatchLabel_GoldenTable
(internal/engine/match_label_test.go) drives the Go side; a JS test pins
the pool-phase rows against the same file.
Schema, one entry per case:
id            the match id exactly as stored (state.MatchResult.ID /
state.BracketMatch.ID)
format        the competition's state.Competition.Format value
("", "mixed", "league", "swiss", "knockout"); only
"league" changes a pool-phase heading ("League table"
instead of the id's own pool name -- CompFormatLeague
reuses the ordinary single-pool match generation, so the
id shape is identical to a real pool's)
label         the expected operator-facing label
matchNumber   KNOCKOUT cases only: state.BracketMatch.MatchNumber for
a synthetic bracket entry at this id (omitted/0 for a
pool-phase case, and for a knockout id no bracket carries
-- MatchLabel's own bare-id fallback then applies)
displayRound  KNOCKOUT cases only: state.BracketMatch.DisplayRound for
the same synthetic entry (1 = Final, see
testdata/round_labels.json for the full table)
Daihyosen/tiebreaker ("-DH-N"/"-TB-N") rows have no JS equivalent to
mirror: poolMatchNumberOf returns 0 for them and scoreRowMatchLabel then
renders no match-number suffix at all (admin_scoring_individual.jsx shows
a separate "DH" tag badge instead). "<pool> daihyosen"/"<pool>
tiebreaker" is this file's OWN spelling for the cases where Go code (a
refusal, a reopen message) must still name the bout in one string; a JS
test consuming these two rows checks that spelling, not an existing
render, since the JS side never had to name one in a single string
before.
